title: Introduce invocation-signature observability adapter and phase-heatmap dashboard with coherence-based alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add invocation signature adapter that correlates logs/traces by compact invocation anchors, new phase-heatmap dashboard, and tuned alert policy using coherence metric to reduce noisy long-tail alerts.
body: Motivation: Long-tail token-cost and latency alerts were noisy because we lacked a lightweight, reliable way to correlate log lines to spans and to attribute cost/latency at the invocation level. This PR introduces an "invocation-signature" adapter and a phase-anchored heatmap dashboard plus an alert-tuning change that uses a coherence score to suppress spurious long-tail noise. Implementation summary: 1) Runtime instrumentation: emit a compact 64-bit invocation.signature computed from stable callsite + prompt-shape hash at invocation start. Instrumentation adds span attributes invocation.signature, kernel.queue_ms, kv.cache_hit, token.estimated_cost and phase.name for per-phase timing. 2) Observability adapter service: a small joiner service that consumes traces and structured logs, joins by invocation.signature within a bounded time window, and emits enriched spans with up to 3 best log excerpts and a coherence_score (0.0-1.0). The adapter is implemented as a new microservice under /observability/signature-joiner and includes a simple in-memory bloom-backed de-dup window to keep collisions low. 3) Dashboards: new panels under Observability -> Invocation Signature Explorer: Phase Heatmap (phase vs. token bucket latency), Token Cost Cohorts, Kernel Queue Waterfall. 4) Alert tuning: a new Alert policy group that attaches a coherence_score filter to SLO-based alerts; alerts with coherence_score < 0.3 are muted by default for 10m to avoid noisy tails. 5) Backwards compatibility: adapter is opt-in via REDWOOD_OBS_SIGNATURE=true; when disabled all instrumentation emits signature=0 and adapter is inactive. Commits summary: three logical commits: (a) runtime: add signature attr and per-phase timing counters,(b) adapter service + unit tests and docs,(c) dashboard panels and alert policy adjustments. Files changed high-level: runtime/instrumentation/*.rs additions to span emitter, observability/signature-joiner service (api, worker, tests), grafana/dashboards/invocation_signature.json, alerts/alert-groups.yaml, docs/obs/signature-adapter.md, sdk/telemetry-shim updates (python/node). Testing and CI: unit tests added for signature hashing and adapter window; integration e2e sim that replays synthetic invocations to validate joins; ci pipeline shows build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-sim: flaky on first run (timeout) then rerun: pass, lint: pass. Performance: signature computation is ~120ns per invocation measured in microbench; adapter adds 0.5ms median enrichment latency but runs asynchronously and does not affect serving path. Review conversation highlights: Reviewer Liam O'Connor requested increasing signature entropy to reduce collision risk and asked for an explicit collision metric in logs; Author (Maya Chen) responded with an updated commit that switches from 64-bit cityhash to a 128-bit murmur3-based truncated xor + callsite salt and added a collision_metrics counter exposed via /metrics. Reviewer Sofia Patel requested that the coherence_score algorithm be documented and have configurable thresholds; updated docs include algorithm summary and OBS_COHERENCE_THRESHOLD env var. Diego Morales tested dashboards and suggested a more compact sparkline for token-cohorts which was applied. Approvals: two approvals after requested changes addressed, then merge. Rollout plan: feature gated and enabled for beta tenants first, ramped to all hosted tenants over two weeks. Observability: added metrics: obs.signature_joins_total, obs.signature_collisions_total, obs.coherence_median, obs.enrichment_latency_ms (p50/p95). Security review: low risk; signature is not derivable to raw PII and adapter respects redaction pipeline. Notes/Followups: track collision rate for 7 days and revisit SLO quiet window length; consider switching adapter to streaming join via Kafka for high-throughput tenants. Merge outcome: merged to main via squash. Linear links: ENG-2314 implements signature adapter, ENG-2390 implements alert tuning. This description is a single continuous string as required by PR metadata.
